org.description: Sennder is a digital road-freight forwarder connecting companies that need to move goods with trucking operators across Europe. Its platform helps customers book, manage and track shipments.

nodes.role: ESG Analyst, MSc company project at SRH Berlin

sections.title: Team project
items: Our team analysed 50 companies’ reported emissions and climate targets to identify potential customers for lower-emission freight services. We compared transport’s share of each company’s footprint and its emissions trend against its stated reduction targets.
Nineteen of the 50 companies had rising emissions, including 16 with SBTi-validated targets. None of the 31 companies in the transport subset had reduced their reported transport emissions.

sections.title: Methods
items: SBTi targets · GHG Protocol · Scope 3 · Freight emissions under EN 16258 · Data validation

nodes.label: GoCarbonTracker
nodes.text: Building a system for reviewing corporate climate disclosures, with reported figures and claims linked to the evidence behind them.

org.description: Corporate climate information is spread across sustainability reports, annual reports, tables and charts. GoCarbonTracker structures that information so a reviewer can find what a company reported, compare disclosures and return to the original evidence. It tracks reported information. It does not independently measure a company’s emissions.

sections.title: Product and review workflow
items: Defined the product requirements and directed AI coding agents to build the workflow, from reading reports and extracting information to retrieving supporting passages and presenting evidence for review. Set traceability as a central requirement: reported figures should link back to their document and page.

sections.title: Document extraction
items: Used coding agents to develop extraction pipelines for emissions figures, climate targets and other information in corporate disclosures. Checked their output against the original reports and investigated failures, including missing table values and chart labels mistaken for data.

sections.title: Company data and relationships
items: Directed the implementation of company records and data-processing tools, including handling earlier names, renames and mergers. The system uses Python and SQL to organise this information.

sections.title: Finding supporting evidence
items: Evaluated five methods for finding relevant passages using the same benchmark. A more elaborate graph-based approach scored below the simpler baseline. Used the results to guide product and implementation decisions.

sections.title: Evaluating apparent contradictions
items: Reviewed every contradiction flagged in one automaker’s reports against the source documents. None was genuine. Used the investigation to identify limitations in the checks and distinguish apparent differences from actual contradictions.

sections.title: Development approach
items: Built GoCarbonTracker through an iterative workflow with AI coding agents. My contribution centres on defining what the system should do, bringing carbon-accounting context to its design, reviewing outputs and directing changes based on tests and source evidence.
Used prompt engineering and multi-agent orchestration to specify tasks and coordinate the development workflow.
